resources.string: Your phone, tablet and laptop sense each other and your hand, using sound too high for you to hear. No internet, no Bluetooth, no account.
Sound travels about 343 metres a second. Two devices trade beeps and time the trip, so they know how far apart they are, to within a few centimetres.
A hand moving closer makes its echo a little higher, and moving away makes it lower. Beep patterns even carry messages between devices.
Every feature hears its sounds through the microphone. Nothing is recorded, saved or sent anywhere.
All set. Your mic is ready to listen.
The microphone is turned off for Nimbat. Turn it on in Settings, then come back here.
The microphone is blocked for this site. Allow it from the site settings next to the address bar, then try again.

Your device hears itself, but this browser hides some of its sounds from the microphone, so measuring distance and sending messages won't work here. Try a different browser for everything.

Your device couldn't hear itself. Turn the device volume up, switch off voice isolation if your mic has it, close anything else using the mic, like dictation or a call, and try somewhere quieter. You can still carry on, but some features may not work.
